overall_notes: This paper focuses on evaluating open-domain story generation by creating better training data for learnable evaluation metrics. The main contribution is generating high-quality implausible stories via plot manipulation and adversarial filtering to train better classifiers (RoBERTa/Longformer) for plausibility assessment. Key finding: metrics trained on their data correlate better with human judgments than heuristic baselines. The LLM-as-judge answer needed correction as this is traditional supervised learning, not the modern LLM-as-judge paradigm.
